name: Mine YouTube comments for buyer objections with Bright Data, OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## The objections nobody puts in your CRM

Nobody tells a vendor why they did not buy. They tell a stranger on YouTube, underneath a review of that vendor's product, at length. "I switched to Craft docs" and "I moved to Workflowy two years back" came from one comment section, and no CRM field will ever hold them.

### How it works

One Bright Data crawl pulls the top comments under every review video you list. **`Sort The Objections`** does the classifying in code, against six rule sets - price, performance, complexity, missing features, switching and trust - and pulls the named alternative out of any comment that says someone left.

**`Rank The Themes`** counts them and weights by likes, because a complaint with 463 likes is a different fact from one with none. The model reads the top quotes per theme and writes one sentence each. It counts nothing, so a garbled reply costs you the prose and not the numbers.

### Setup

1. A **Bright Data** credential as HTTP Header Auth: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`.

2. Put competitor review video URLs in `video_urls` in **Settings**, one per line or comma separated.

3. `comments_per_video` matters more than it looks. Leave it empty and the API returns **one** comment after nearly three minutes.

4. A Google Sheet with the columns `run_date`, `theme`, `comments`, `likes`, `share_pct` and `top_quote`.

5. An OpenAI credential and a Slack credential.

## 1. Which comment sections
Competitor review videos. `comments_per_video` is the field that matters - leave it empty and the API returns one comment in 164 seconds.

## 2. One crawl for every video
Three videos at 40 comments each took 23 seconds, so it polls rather than waiting on a synchronous call.

## 3. Errors arrive as rows
A video that returned nothing is a row with `error` and no comment text - and it can be the first one in the array.

## 4. Six rule sets, in code
Price, performance, complexity, missing features, switching and trust. The named alternative comes out of whatever the person actually typed.

## 5. Words, not numbers
The model writes one sentence per theme and counts nothing, so a garbled reply costs the prose and never the totals.

## 6. A row per theme, a digest per run
The Split Out is what stops the sheet getting one row whose columns are `message` and `rows`.

## Errors arrive as rows

A video that fails comes back inside the results array as a row with `error` and no `comment_text` - and it can be the first one. `Read The Comments` separates them and names the video rather than letting the count quietly shrink.
